title: Bakery costing and customer quotes
intro: Turn recipe notes into a cost picture you can review before sending a quote.
items: Build a recipe ingredient-cost sheet
Start with purchase records and compatible units before deciding what to charge.

Turn these fictional ingredient records into a costing table: [pack price, pack quantity, recipe usage, unit]. Show cost per unit and recipe contribution for each ingredient. Flag incompatible or missing units. Do not invent purchase prices.
Independently check one ingredient calculation and every unit conversion.
Cost an order that needs whole batches
An order above one recipe yield may require another complete batch.

A recipe yields [12] units and an order needs [14]. List whole batches, total units made and spare units. Allocate the entered batch costs to this order. Show the formula and do not assume spare units will sell.
For this example, two batches make 24 units and leave 10 spare.
Account for hands-on baking time
Your preparation, finishing and cleanup time belong in the review.

Organize these task notes into preparation, production, decoration and cleanup: [fictional notes]. Separate batch-level hours from order-level hours. Using my chosen rate [amount per hour], show the labour calculation. Ask about gaps instead of choosing a wage for me.
Check that order-level time is not multiplied by the batch count.
Check packaging cost per order
Boxes and boards can be counted differently from individual baked items.

Create a packaging checklist for [order description]. Use only these quantities and costs: [records]. Distinguish per-item wrapping, per-box packaging and one-off boards. Calculate totals and mark missing items as unknown rather than free.
Reconcile the number of boxes with their capacity and the order quantity.
Explain margin versus markup with my figures
Two percentages can describe different amounts even when the numbers sound similar.

Using a fictional included cost of [1000], compare adding a [25]% markup with targeting a [25]% margin on selling price. Show each formula, selling price and difference from cost. State that omitted expenses are not included in these scenarios.
A 25% markup gives 1250; a 25% margin scenario is about 1333.33.
Review costs missing from a cake quote
A short review can reveal assumptions before a customer sees the price.

Review this fictional cake quote and cost list: [redacted example]. Create columns for included, excluded and unknown costs. Check delivery, decoration time, packaging, payment charges and taxes without deciding legal treatment. Return questions for the owner, not an asserted final price.
Resolve unknowns against your own records before relying on the quote.
Draft a clear custom-cake enquiry reply
Collect the details needed to understand the order before offering a quote.

Draft a friendly reply to a cake enquiry for [occasion]. Ask for date, servings, flavour, design reference, collection or delivery and dietary requirements to discuss. Do not promise availability, allergen safety or a price. Keep it under 100 words.
Confirm your actual availability and ingredient information yourself.
Make a deposit and balance summary
Keep the agreed quote total separate from the amounts already paid.

Format a fictional quote of [2400], deposit received [600] and next payment date [date] into a customer summary. Show total, payments received and remaining balance. Include placeholders for the seller's actual payment and cancellation terms; do not invent policy.
The example balance is 1800; the deposit does not reduce the agreed total.
Compare two cake decoration options
A clear scope comparison makes it easier to explain different quotes.

Compare these two proposed decoration scopes: [option A] and [option B]. Build a customer-facing table of size, finish, custom elements, delivery and stated price. Use only supplied facts. Follow it with a short neutral explanation of what differs, without calling either option better value.
Check that photos or references match the finish you can actually supply.
Review estimated versus actual order costs
Past orders can help identify which assumptions need attention next time.

Compare this fictional estimate with recorded order costs and time: [two tables]. Show differences for ingredients, labour, packaging and delivery. List possible explanations as questions, not facts. Suggest which records to capture for the next similar order without predicting profit.
Use actual receipts and time records to confirm each difference.

title: Salon content and booking conversations
intro: Create practical content from your real services, hours and filming capacity.
items: Plan a week of salon posts
Start with services you actually provide and footage you can realistically capture.

Plan seven content slots for a salon offering [services] in [area]. Use three educational posts, two service explainers, one team introduction and one booking reminder. Include a purpose, needed footage and draft caption for each. Do not invent discounts, testimonials or availability.
Match every named service and booking detail to your current menu.
Explain a salon service without medical claims
A useful explainer tells a customer what happens and what to ask.

Write a plain-language explanation of [service] using these approved notes: [facts]. Cover the appointment steps, approximate duration if supplied and questions a client can ask. Avoid medical advice, guaranteed results and claims about curing hair or skin conditions.
Have the service provider review suitability statements and promised outcomes.
Turn one salon topic into a reel shot list
A small filming brief is easier to execute than a vague request to make content.

Create a six-shot vertical reel plan about [salon topic]. Use only [available spaces and equipment]. For each shot, give action, framing, on-screen text and the information it communicates. Keep clients out of frame unless separate permission and production arrangements are confirmed.
Check reflections and backgrounds for people or appointment details.
Draft an appointment enquiry reply
A booking reply should help the customer take one clear next step.

Draft a response to an enquiry about [service]. Ask for preferred day and time and explain our actual booking route [link or phone]. Use the supplied duration and starting-price facts only. Do not confirm a slot until the salon checks its calendar.
Verify the booking link, service duration and any displayed starting price.
Adapt a salon caption into natural Hinglish
Adapt the tone while preserving the actual facts and next step.

Rewrite this English salon caption in conversational Roman-script Hinglish: [caption]. Keep the service name, booking link and policy unchanged. Give one English and one Hinglish version, each under 80 words. Avoid stereotypes, exaggerated beauty promises and invented local slang.
Ask someone familiar with your customers' language to review the phrasing.
Write a consultation preparation post
Help customers arrive with useful questions rather than a promised result.

Draft a carousel outline explaining how to prepare for a [service] consultation. Use these salon-approved notes [notes]. Suggest questions about goals, upkeep, time and costs. Do not assess a person's condition, prescribe treatment or guarantee the result from a reference photo.
Remove any recommendation the qualified service provider has not approved.
Create an honest cancellation reminder
Existing policy can be explained clearly without adding pressure.

Rewrite this actual cancellation policy [policy] as a friendly reminder for a booking confirmation. Preserve notice periods, fees and exceptions exactly. If any term is ambiguous, list it as a question for the owner. Do not add penalties or claim an appointment is already paid.
Compare the draft line by line with the policy customers agreed to.
Plan salon footage without filming clients
Spaces, tools and demonstrations can explain the experience on their own.

Suggest ten shots for a salon content session using [available rooms, tools and consenting team members]. Exclude identifiable clients, customer records and private conversations. Group the shots into welcome, process and team themes. Avoid staging a result as a real customer transformation.
Check mirrors, screens, paperwork and audio before recording.
Answer common salon pricing questions
A precise answer explains the quote process and its limits.

Using our real service menu [menu], draft answers to five common pricing questions. Distinguish fixed prices from starting prices and consultation quotes. State only supplied inclusions and conditions. If a fee is missing, say the salon must confirm it rather than estimating.
Make sure customers can tell what the displayed price actually includes.
Build a salon content approval checklist
A short approval step helps prevent errors in otherwise polished posts.

Create a one-page pre-publication checklist for salon posts. Cover service facts, prices, booking links, client permissions, misleading editing, readable text and owner approval. Add spaces for reviewer, date and corrections. Keep each check observable rather than asking whether content is simply good.
Assign a person who can verify the service facts before publishing.

title: Website briefs and page improvements
intro: Give an AI coding tool specific requirements and review the result one section at a time.
items: Write a useful website project brief
A focused brief gives the builder enough context to make coherent decisions.

Turn these business notes [notes] into a website brief. Specify audience, primary task, page list, tone, available assets and required integrations. Separate confirmed facts from open questions. End with five observable acceptance checks. Do not invent testimonials, client logos or business results.
Confirm the main customer task before choosing visual effects.
Improve a landing-page hero
Help a visitor understand the offer and the next action quickly.

Review this hero copy [copy] for [audience]. Rewrite it with a concrete headline, one explanatory sentence and a clear primary action. Use only the supplied product facts. Offer three directions with different emphasis, and explain what each one helps the visitor understand.
Check that the headline describes something the actual product delivers.
Plan a readable product-page layout
Arrange information around what a buyer needs to decide.

Outline a product page for [product] using this verified file list, outcome and requirements [facts]. Include an actual preview, scope, price, delivery explanation and questions buyers may have. Specify which missing information needs owner input. Do not add scarcity or social proof we cannot substantiate.
Make files, requirements and purchase terms easy to find before checkout.
Translate a visual reference into design rules
Extract reusable layout principles while keeping your own assets and identity.

Describe the layout principles in this reference [description]: spacing, typography hierarchy, section rhythm and image treatment. Turn them into an original direction for [brand]. Do not copy the reference's text, illustrations, logos or distinctive branded artwork. Include a small-screen adaptation plan.
Use assets you own or have permission to use.
Specify accessible form behaviour
A form brief should describe labels, errors and successful completion.

Write requirements for a [contact or quote] form with [fields]. Define visible labels, required fields, validation messages, keyboard order, error focus and a success state. Ask which system receives the submission. Do not invent a working integration or call the form accessible without testing it.
Test completion and error recovery using only a keyboard.
Make mobile product cards easier to scan
Keep the essentials visible at narrow widths.

Review this product-card markup and CSS [code]. Suggest the smallest changes to preserve image ratio, readable title, short summary, USD-first price with the supplied INR alternative and a clear link at 390 px width. Preserve existing destinations and actual amounts. Explain any overflow cause.
Check actual rendered cards for clipping, wrapping and keyboard focus.
Write an honest FAQ for a digital download
Answer buying questions from verified product information.

Using this product specification [facts], draft six FAQs about included files, software requirements, licence, payment, delivery and refunds. Keep answers short. Flag missing policies for the owner instead of inventing them. Do not imply a subscription, lifetime updates or support commitment unless stated.
Make every answer agree with the actual checkout and policy pages.
Describe a restrained website animation
Motion should support the content and respect a visitor's preferences.

Specify one subtle animation for [section] on [website type]. Define its purpose, duration, trigger and final state. Include reduced-motion behaviour and a fully readable state when animation fails. Avoid making essential copy depend on a scroll effect or delaying the primary action.
Test the page with reduced motion enabled and JavaScript unavailable.
Review a page before publishing
A bounded checklist makes a release review more practical.

Create a release checklist for this static page [summary]. Cover headings, actual local links, image alternatives, mobile overflow, form behaviour, prices and metadata. Give a concrete test for each item and a place to record evidence. Separate checks that need account access from local checks.
Record failures and fixes; a checklist alone does not establish that tests passed.
Write a page title and description
Search metadata should describe what a visitor will actually find.

Draft five unique titles and descriptions for this page [actual content and audience]. Emphasize the main task, use natural wording and avoid unsupported superlatives. Keep the brand concise. Flag any proposed wording that the page does not substantiate; do not promise rankings or rich results.
Choose wording that matches the page's visible heading and content.

title: Carousels and useful social posts
intro: Move from a real audience question to a coherent sequence of slides.
items: Outline a six-slide educational carousel
Give each slide one job and make the sequence answer a real question.

Build a six-slide outline answering [audience question] using these verified notes [notes]. Use a clear cover, four teaching slides and one practical next step. Give each slide a headline, short body and visual suggestion. Mark evidence gaps instead of filling them with invented statistics.
Read only the slide headlines to see whether the sequence still makes sense.
Write a specific carousel cover
A clear promise helps the right reader decide whether to continue.

Write ten cover headlines for a carousel about [topic] for [audience]. Each must describe the actual lesson in [outline]. Avoid income promises, fear-based pressure and claims that everyone makes the same mistake. Group the options into question, checklist and worked-example approaches.
The remaining slides must deliver the exact lesson promised on the cover.
Reduce text on crowded carousel slides
Shorten the explanation while preserving the part that makes it accurate.

Edit this carousel slide text [text] into a short headline and no more than three concise supporting points. Preserve qualifications, units and conditions. List any detail moved to the caption. If the topic cannot fit responsibly, recommend splitting the slide rather than removing essential context.
Compare the shortened version with the original for changes in meaning.
Turn a worked example into a carousel
A sequence can teach a process without claiming the example is typical.

Turn this fictional worked example [example] into six slides. Label it fictional, show inputs before outputs and explain one step per slide. Keep calculations visible where needed. Finish with a question readers can use on their own records, not a promised result or earnings claim.
Recalculate every displayed number independently.
Define a consistent carousel visual system
A small set of rules can hold different slides together.

Propose a visual system for [brand] and [carousel topic]: two type sizes, spacing rules, accent colours and a repeated footer position. Explain how examples, warnings and steps will differ. Use our available fonts and assets [list]. Include a contrast and mobile readability review.
Inspect the exported slides on an actual small screen.
Draft useful carousel image descriptions
Describe the information that matters rather than repeating a filename.

Draft image descriptions for these carousel slides [slide text and visual descriptions]. Preserve meaningful relationships in charts or diagrams and identify slide order where helpful. Avoid claims about details not supplied. Flag slides whose text is too dense to describe clearly without redesign.
Check descriptions against the finished export, not just the original outline.
Write a caption that adds context
The caption can supply conditions and sources that do not belong on the cover.

Write a caption for this carousel [outline]. Add one useful example, relevant limitations and a simple next step. Use these sources only [sources], identifying anything not verified. Do not repeat every slide or invent engagement, testimonials or customer outcomes. Keep the tone [tone].
Make the caption useful even if the reader does not respond or buy.
Repurpose a blog lesson into a carousel
Choose one coherent lesson rather than squeezing a complete article into slides.

From this original article [text], identify three possible carousel lessons. Recommend the one that can be explained accurately in six slides. Draft the chosen outline and list details that need to remain in the linked article. Preserve source attributions and do not add new factual claims.
Check that the carousel links to the correct article and preserves its context.
Prepare a carousel handoff for a designer
A handoff should separate approved content from visual choices still to make.

Format this approved carousel outline [outline] as a production brief. For every slide list headline, body, evidence reference, visual direction and export note. Mark unresolved questions clearly. Add an approval checklist for factual accuracy, rights, readability and destination links before publication.
Confirm the final slide numbers match the export order.
Plan a fair carousel hook test
Change one element so the comparison is easier to interpret.

Design a small test comparing these two truthful carousel covers [A and B] with the same remaining slides. Identify the reader action to measure and the conditions to keep similar. Explain likely confounders and a review plan. Do not invent sample sizes, statistical confidence or expected improvement.
Use actual platform data and comparable time windows when reviewing results.

title: Short videos and character stories
intro: Prepare a story, shots and review notes before spending time on production.
items: Write a compact two-character reel story
A small problem and a clear turn are enough for a short scene.

Write an original approximately 100-word story for two fictional characters [traits] about [everyday problem]. Use setup, misunderstanding, correction and a final action. Keep locations and props limited to [available assets]. Avoid borrowing recognisable characters, catchphrases or scenes from existing entertainment.
Read it aloud and check whether the action fits the intended duration.
Turn a script into a shot list
Describe what the viewer sees at each step.

Convert this original script [script] into a shot list. For each shot specify character action, framing, dialogue, relevant prop and transition. Keep screen direction consistent. Flag actions that the available scene or character rig [limitations] cannot perform instead of assuming extra assets exist.
Match every spoken line and important action to an actual shot.
Build a reusable character continuity sheet
Repeated details help a series stay coherent across separate scenes.

Create a continuity sheet for these original characters [descriptions]. Record appearance, proportions, wardrobe, voice direction, habitual gestures and important props. Separate fixed traits from episode-specific changes. Do not imitate a real person's voice or introduce design details not approved by the creator.
Compare each render with the approved character references.
Review a short-video opening
Make the situation understandable before adding more visual complexity.

Review the first five seconds of this script [opening] for [audience]. Give three revisions that establish the situation and reason to keep watching. Use only what the video actually delivers. Avoid fake urgency, fabricated danger or exaggerated promises. Explain the information each version conveys.
Watch the opening without sound to see what the image communicates.
Plan captions that remain readable
Caption timing and placement need review on the finished video.

Using this transcript [text] and planned duration [duration], suggest short caption groups and line breaks. Preserve the speaker's meaning and important names. Identify moments requiring extra reading time. Leave room for platform controls and important faces; do not invent precise timings without the actual audio.
Check caption timing and placement against the rendered audio and frames.
Make a vertical-video framing checklist
Important details can disappear when a landscape scene becomes vertical.

Create a framing review for this vertical video plan [shots]. Identify the subject, essential action and readable text in each shot. Suggest what to remove or reposition when space is tight. Flag reliance on platform-specific safe areas that must be checked in the current publishing preview.
Preview on the actual platform before publishing rather than trusting a generic overlay.
Write voice direction without imitation
Describe delivery in ordinary terms that a performer can use.

Write voice direction for this original dialogue [dialogue]. Specify pace, emotional intention, pauses and pronunciation notes. Give character distinctions through delivery rather than copying a named actor or real person's voice. Keep the instructions consistent with the meaning of each line.
Listen to the complete scene for clarity, pronunciation and balanced levels.
Create three episodes from one reusable set
Shared production constraints can support a repeatable series.

Suggest three original episodes for [two character descriptions] using only [set and props]. Give each a different problem, turning point and final action. Keep the production scope similar across episodes and label any required new asset. Do not promise that any premise will go viral.
Confirm the episodes differ in the actual story, not only in the title.
Prepare an edit review with timecoded notes
Specific notes make revisions easier to act on.

Convert these rough review notes [notes] into an edit list with fields for timecode, observed issue, requested change and verification. Preserve unknown timecodes as placeholders. Separate factual errors, audio issues, caption problems and optional style changes. Do not mark a fix complete without evidence.
Check the revised export against each note and record unresolved items.
Write a useful video description
A description can explain scope and provide the next practical step.

Draft a title and description for this finished video [transcript and summary]. Describe what is actually shown, credit supplied assets [credits] and include this relevant next-step link [link]. Clearly label fictional demonstrations. Do not imply the video proves business outcomes or endorses a tool officially.
Verify links and credits against the files used in the final export.

title: UGC scripts and product demonstrations
intro: Build a script around demonstrable product facts and footage you can actually produce.
items: Separate product facts from advertising claims
Start with a record of what you can substantiate.

Review this product brief [brief]. Create columns for supplied fact, proposed claim, available evidence and unresolved question. Distinguish features from possible customer outcomes. Do not approve claims, invent studies or assume that a review represents all buyers. Flag statements needing qualified or platform-specific review.
Have the owner approve the evidence for every claim before production.
Write a demonstration-led UGC script
Show a real action that supports the explanation.

Draft a short UGC-style script for [product] using these verified facts [facts]. Structure it as situation, demonstration, limitation and next step. Pair every sentence with producible footage. Do not write a first-person customer experience unless the actual creator can truthfully say it.
Match each claim to the exact action visible in the footage.
Generate truthful hook options for one product
Different openings can highlight different uses of the same real feature.

Write twelve hooks for [product] and [audience] using only [verified features]. Group them by problem explanation, demonstration and comparison. Avoid invented testimonials, fake scarcity, income guarantees and unsupported superiority claims. Identify which opening shot each hook requires.
Reject hooks that would need footage or evidence you do not have.
Plan a product unboxing shot sequence
A clear sequence shows what is actually included.

Create an unboxing shot list from this verified package inventory [list]. Show outer packaging, each included item and relevant setup steps. Distinguish optional accessories from included items. Suggest clean framing and readable labels without adding branded elements or packaging that the delivered product lacks.
Compare the shot plan with a real order before filming.
Draft a product comparison using known facts
A useful comparison states its criteria and the information gaps.

Build a comparison of [option A] and [option B] from these dated specifications [records]. Use the same criteria for both and cite the supplied source for each fact. Mark unknowns. Avoid declaring a universal winner or implying that a higher price automatically means better quality.
Recheck changeable specifications against the current seller pages before publication.
Explain who a product may suit
Clear fit and limitations help a buyer make an informed decision.

Using this verified product scope [scope], draft a short section describing suitable use cases, required tools and situations it does not cover. Avoid assumptions about a reader's health, finances or personal circumstances. Make the language invitational and factual, with no guaranteed results.
Keep the exclusions as easy to find as the benefits.
Storyboard a six-shot product ad
Each shot should carry a specific piece of information.

Storyboard six shots for [product] using [available footage and props]. Give action, framing, spoken line, on-screen text and the verified fact conveyed. Include a real product view and a clear purchase destination. Label any conceptual illustration so it is not mistaken for product evidence.
Check that generated or staged imagery does not misrepresent the actual product.
Write a creator brief with honest boundaries
A creator needs both the message and the claims they should not make.

Draft a creator brief for [product]. Include approved facts, supplied evidence, prohibited unsupported claims, deliverables, available assets and review steps. Ask the owner for applicable sponsorship-disclosure requirements rather than inventing them. Do not require a creator to pretend to be an unaffiliated customer.
Agree on truthful disclosure and usage permissions before publishing.
Review an ad script for unsupported promises
Polished language can still overstate what a product does.

Review this draft ad script [script] against these approved product facts [facts]. Highlight each unsupported statement and propose a narrower truthful version. Identify missing conditions, implied guarantees and invented experiences. Preserve useful concrete demonstrations. Do not label the result legally compliant or platform-approved.
Send unresolved claims and disclosure questions to the appropriate reviewer.
Plan an ad creative test from a real hypothesis
A test is easier to learn from when the intended change is clear.

Write a creative test plan for this product [facts]. Compare a demonstration opening with a question opening while keeping the offer and destination constant. Define the hypothesis, actual event to measure and review conditions. Do not choose a budget, predict returns or invent confidence from missing data.
Verify measurement and obtain a spending limit before activating any campaign.

title: Recurring bills and financial organisation
intro: Organise redacted records and questions; keep decisions and account access under your control.
items: Organise an anonymised recurring-bill ledger
A ledger is easier to review when sources and billing periods stay attached.

Turn these fictional billing records [redacted rows] into a table with provider label, amount, currency, billing period, renewal date and source reference. Keep different currencies separate. Flag missing periods or uncertain dates. Do not infer account numbers, access accounts or recommend financial products.
Verify every amount and date against the original record.
Compare monthly and annual billing amounts
Comparisons need equivalent periods and stated assumptions.

Compare these fictional monthly and annual subscription offers [records]. Show a twelve-month baseline for monthly billing and identify setup fees, tax treatment or renewal terms as unknown unless supplied. Keep currencies separate and do not choose a plan for me or assume I will use it all year.
Check commitment periods and actual renewal pricing before deciding.
Flag possible duplicate subscriptions
Two similar records are a reason to investigate, not proof of waste.

Review this anonymised subscription list [list] for possible overlapping purpose, repeated provider labels or duplicate entries. Explain why each item needs review and what evidence would resolve it. Do not assume separate subscriptions are unnecessary or instruct cancellation without owner confirmation.
Confirm account ownership and actual usage before treating an item as redundant.
Create a renewal-date review list
A simple record can make upcoming decisions easier to see.

Organise these redacted renewal records [records] by stated renewal date. Include provider alias, notice deadline if explicitly supplied, amount, currency and source. Flag ambiguous dates. Do not infer a cancellation window from the renewal date or claim that an external reminder has been created.
Enter and verify any reminders yourself in the system you actually use.
Draft questions about an unexplained charge
A neutral enquiry can ask for evidence without alleging wrongdoing.

Draft a polite billing enquiry about this fictional charge [provider alias, date, amount and issue]. Ask for the billed service, covered period and relevant invoice. Use placeholders for private account details. Do not accuse fraud, claim a legal entitlement or send the message on my behalf.
Use the provider's verified contact route and insert private details yourself.
Prepare a subscription review agenda
A short agenda helps the owner make the final decisions.

Create a review agenda from this anonymised service list [list]. Group questions under use, upcoming renewal, overlaps and alternatives to investigate. Add a decision column with keep, review or ask-provider options. Do not estimate savings, cancel services or treat missing usage data as zero usage.
Record the owner's actual decision and its evidence separately from the draft.
Compare two invoices for a price change
Comparable line items matter more than a simple total difference.

Compare these fictional invoices [A and B]. Align service period, quantity, unit rate, discount and other stated charges. Calculate differences only for comparable entries. Explain unknown or changed scope. Do not label a higher total an error without checking whether the service or period changed.
Reconcile the line items with both original invoices.
Write a negotiation enquiry without invented leverage
Ask about available options using accurate account history.

Draft a polite renewal enquiry using these facts [redacted service and history]. Ask whether currently available plans or billing options better match [needs]. Do not fabricate a competitor quote, loyalty period, hardship claim or intention to cancel. Leave the final decision and sending to me.
Verify every statement about your history before using the draft.
Summarise a cancellation policy for review
A summary should preserve conditions and point back to the source.

Summarise this supplied cancellation policy [text] into notice period, required channel, stated fees, exclusions and unanswered questions. Quote no more than the short phrases needed for accuracy. Identify ambiguity rather than resolving it as legal advice. Do not claim cancellation has been completed.
Read the current policy and verify completion directly with the provider.
Create a bill-review record that avoids sensitive data
A review worksheet can use aliases instead of full account information.

Design a bill-review worksheet with provider alias, service category, amount, currency, period, source reference, open question and owner decision. Exclude passwords, payment-card details and account identifiers. Add a field for the reviewer to confirm the original record was checked; do not populate fictional decisions as real ones.
Keep the source documents in your chosen secure system, not in a public prompt.

title: Wedding planning and vendor comparisons
intro: Compare supplied facts and organise decisions while checking actual vendor terms yourself.
items: Compare wedding vendor quotes on the same basis
A headline price may leave important scope differences unexplained.

Compare these fictional wedding vendor quotes [A and B] in one table. Include date, hours, guest count, deliverables, travel, stated extras and payment schedule. Mark missing details as unknown. Use one supplied currency per comparison and do not declare a best vendor from price alone.
Confirm availability and all inclusions directly with each vendor.
Draft a venue enquiry with useful details
A specific enquiry helps a venue explain its actual offer.

Draft a venue enquiry for [fictional date, approximate guest count and event format]. Ask about availability, included spaces, access times, food arrangements, accessibility information and written quote terms. Do not share guest identities or assume a listed package includes every required service.
Replace example dates and confirm what the written quote actually covers.
Identify wedding quote details to clarify
Unknowns should become questions before a deposit is paid.

Review this redacted vendor quote [quote]. List questions about coverage hours, deliverables, additional charges, payment dates, rescheduling and cancellation terms. Distinguish missing information from an unfavourable term. Do not interpret enforceability or advise signing; ask for written clarification where needed.
Use qualified advice for contract questions beyond the supplied wording.
Organise wedding deposits and balances
Track payments against their own source records and due dates.

Turn these fictional vendor records [records] into a payment tracker. Include agreed total, recorded payments, remaining balance, stated due date and receipt reference. Flag missing receipts and mismatched totals. Do not assume a deposit is refundable or combine different currencies into one total.
Reconcile every payment with a receipt or confirmed bank record.
Build a wedding guest-count worksheet
Planning counts can use anonymous groups instead of personal guest data.

Create a guest-count worksheet from these fictional group totals [counts]. Separate invited, confirmed, declined and awaiting response. Include adult and child counts only if supplied. Show reconciliation questions where categories overlap. Do not infer meal needs, relationships or personal details.
Check that every person belongs to one response category before using totals.
Draft a wedding planning task list
A task list works better when responsibility and dependency are visible.

Turn these wedding planning notes [anonymised notes] into tasks with owner role, due date placeholder, dependency and completion evidence. Separate decisions from actions. Do not invent deadlines based on assumed vendor practices. Identify items whose timing needs confirmation from a real supplier.
Agree actual deadlines and responsibilities with the people involved.
Compare two wedding menu proposals
Compare quantities and service arrangements alongside the stated price.

Compare these fictional menu proposals [menus and supplied prices]. List guest basis, courses, service style, drinks, equipment and stated exclusions. Mark dietary and allergen information that must be confirmed with the caterer. Avoid asserting that a menu is safe for a particular guest.
Ask the caterer directly about dietary requirements and cross-contact procedures.
Prepare a photographer deliverables checklist
Written scope helps distinguish event coverage from the final files.

Create a clarification checklist from this fictional photography proposal [proposal]. Cover attendance hours, photographer count, editing scope, delivery format, delivery timing, usage terms and stated extra charges. Preserve unknowns. Do not assume ownership or publication permissions beyond the actual agreement.
Confirm the final deliverables and image-use permissions in writing.
Make a wedding-day handoff sheet
A handoff sheet should identify who handles a task without exposing extra data.

Draft a wedding-day handoff template for [event outline]. Use role labels for suppliers and helpers, with fields for confirmed timing, location, dependency and escalation contact to fill privately. Do not place real phone numbers in the prompt or assume suppliers share personal information with one another.
Verify the handoff details with each responsible person before distributing.
Review wedding scope changes before approval
A change can affect several linked parts of a vendor quote.

Compare this original fictional scope [A] with the proposed revision [B]. List changes to quantity, time, deliverables, price and payment dates. Separate confirmed changes from assumptions and draft clarification questions. Do not approve the change, calculate legal liability or imply a refund right.
Use the updated written agreement as the source for approved terms.

title: Shared household administration
intro: Use fictional records to design neutral worksheets; keep personal and family information private.
items: Build a neutral shared-expense worksheet
A useful record separates the expense from assumptions about who owes it.

Design a worksheet using these fictional shared expenses [rows]. Include description, date, amount, currency, receipt reference, agreed allocation rule and payment status. Leave unknown allocation rules blank. Do not infer responsibility from relationships, rewrite agreements or provide legal advice.
Use only allocation rules that the relevant people have already agreed.
Separate factual notes from interpretations
Neutral records describe observable events and preserve their source.

Rewrite these fictional administrative notes [notes] into date, observed event, source reference and follow-up question. Separate direct observations from interpretations. Do not label anyone's character, infer motives or present a summary as an authenticated transcript. Keep the original source unchanged.
Compare the draft with the original record and retain any relevant uncertainty.
Prepare a household handoff checklist
A checklist can reduce forgotten items without judging anyone involved.

Draft a neutral handoff checklist for [fictional household arrangement]. Group items under belongings, documents, confirmed timing and questions to resolve. Use role placeholders rather than names. Do not infer medical needs, change existing arrangements or introduce obligations that were not supplied.
Confirm the list matches the existing arrangement and actual required items.
Organise an agreed household schedule
An administrative table should preserve the schedule it is based on.

Format this fictional agreed schedule [schedule] into a table with date, time, location placeholder and responsible role. Flag overlapping or missing entries. Do not choose between conflicting instructions or modify an agreement. Exclude personal addresses and ask for clarification wherever the supplied record is inconsistent.
Verify dates, time zones and changes against the original agreement.
Draft a neutral administrative message
State a concrete question and the relevant facts without assigning blame.

Draft a brief message about this fictional scheduling issue [facts]. State the known date and time, the unresolved question and a proposed way to confirm the arrangement. Avoid accusations, inferred motives or legal assertions. Do not send the message or imply the other person has agreed.
Read the draft for accuracy and tone before deciding whether to use it.
Check a shared-expense allocation example
Arithmetic can be checked independently of whether an allocation was agreed.

For a fictional expense of [120] with a supplied agreed split of [60/40], show each share and reconciliation to the total. Keep currencies separate. Explain that the calculation applies only to the entered rule and does not establish who is legally responsible for payment.
The example shares are 72 and 48; verify the rule separately.
Create a document reference register
A register can point to private files without copying their contents.

Create a household document register template with document label, source date, version, private storage reference and review status. Use fictional labels only. Exclude names, addresses, identification numbers and confidential contents. Explain how to mark a newer version without deleting or silently changing the original record.
Store actual documents in the secure location you choose and control.
Turn open household questions into a review agenda
A short agenda can distinguish a missing fact from a pending decision.

Organise these fictional household admin questions [questions] into records to check, details to confirm and decisions requiring agreement. Add a source field and responsible role placeholder. Do not resolve disputes, infer consent or prioritise one person's preferences as binding instructions.
Record confirmed answers separately from proposals or unresolved questions.
Prepare a private-record backup checklist
A checklist should describe real actions instead of claiming a backup exists.

Draft a backup checklist for private household worksheets. Include choosing storage, access review, dated copies, a restoration check and a review of accidental sharing. Do not name an unverified storage service as secure or imply files have been copied. Keep credentials and actual file contents out of the prompt.
Perform a restore check with a harmless sample before relying on a backup.
Review a household worksheet for oversharing
Keep the record focused on the administrative task it serves.

Review this fictional worksheet schema [field names only]. Identify fields unnecessary for [administrative purpose], sensitive free-text areas and places where source references could replace copied personal details. Suggest a simpler version. Do not request actual family records or make decisions about legal retention obligations.
Review access and sharing with the people responsible for the actual records.

title: Digital products and small-business offers
intro: Clarify what you sell, show the actual files and test the buying experience.
items: Define a small digital product around one task
A bounded task makes it easier to explain and verify the product.

From these audience problems [notes], propose three small digital products that each help complete one specific task. For each, state buyer, input, output, included files, required tools and exclusions. Do not invent demand data, sales forecasts or claim the idea is validated by this exercise.
Talk to potential buyers and test a real sample before treating the idea as validated.
Write a precise digital-product file list
Customers should know what they will download before paying.

Turn this actual archive inventory [filenames and descriptions] into a customer file list. Group guides, templates, examples and software separately. State editable formats and required tools only when supplied. Flag missing instructions or ambiguous licences instead of promising compatibility with untested apps.
Unzip the actual customer archive and verify every listed file exists.
Design a free sample that demonstrates the task
A sample can show the working method with clear scope.

Suggest a useful free sample for this product [verified scope]. Define one complete exercise, fictional input and a way to check the output. Explain what the paid product adds without withholding a step required for the free exercise to work. Avoid promising results beyond the supplied tool.
Complete the sample as a new user with only the published instructions.
Draft a digital-product sales page from facts
A good page connects the customer's task with what the files actually provide.

Draft a product page using these confirmed facts [scope, files, requirements and price]. Include who it suits, a preview description, first-use steps, limitations and purchase details. Mark missing information for the owner. Do not invent reviews, earnings, urgency, guarantees or a support commitment.
Check the copy against the real files, checkout and licence before release.
Explain fixed USD and INR prices consistently
The display order can change while the actual regional offers remain fixed.

Using these exact fixed prices [USD amount] and [INR amount], draft a product-card price label with USD first and a smaller or INR alternative. State one-time payment only if confirmed. Do not calculate exchange rates, invent discounts or change the amounts to make them appear equivalent.
Compare both labels with the server-owned checkout amounts.
Prepare a first-use README for a download
A new buyer needs to know which file to open and what to expect.

Write a README from this actual bundle inventory and setup process [facts]. Include download, unzip, first file to open, a fictional worked example, save or export steps and known limitations. Distinguish local actions from any external service. Do not describe untested compatibility as verified.
Follow the README on a clean test setup and record where instructions are missing.
Review a product cover for misleading cues
A cover should help a buyer recognise the actual offer.

Review this cover concept [description] against these product facts [facts]. Flag implied physical shipping, software access, video lessons or included assets that the download does not provide. Suggest a clearer title, subtitle and format label. Do not add ratings, bestseller badges or customer counts without evidence.
Use actual previews to explain the files alongside any conceptual cover artwork.
Build a digital-download purchase test checklist
A purchase test needs to include failures as well as the happy path.

Create a test checklist for this existing digital-download flow [steps]. Cover displayed amounts, selected currency, cancelled payment, failed verification, successful confirmation, download and support instructions. Use test payments and fictional data. Do not execute a charge or report a payment as verified without server evidence.
Confirm the downloaded archive matches the file the product page promises.
Turn customer questions into useful blog topics
Actual questions can suggest content with a concrete purpose.

Group these anonymised pre-purchase questions [questions] by the task the reader is trying to complete. Propose article titles and a useful worked exercise for each group. Link each proposal to an actual product capability only where relevant. Do not invent keyword volume or assume a topic will rank.
Use real search and customer evidence to prioritise which article to produce first.
Review a product launch with evidence
A review should distinguish observed behaviour from hoped-for results.

Create a launch review template for [product]. Separate traffic, product views, checkout starts, verified purchases, delivery issues and feedback. Add source, date range and uncertainty fields. Do not fabricate conversion rates, attribute sales to an ad without evidence or infer success from visits alone.
Calculate rates from matching event definitions and comparable date ranges.
